title: ReMoVe: Refining a Video Model's Own Motion for Coherent Human Video Generation
abstract: arXiv:2611.18666v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Video generation models have become increasingly capable of synthesizing realistic human motion, yet they often lose track of the very structure that makes the motion plausible. As generated human motion becomes more complex, videos can suffer from progressive body deformation and appearance drift across frames. Existing motion-controlled methods use explicit representations to stabilize generation, but typically rely on pre-defined motion sequences as references. This raises a fundamental question: if the base generator already produces a usable coarse motion, why replace it with an external one? ReMoVe answers this question by treating the coarse output as a motion hypothesis rather than a final result. ReMoVe recovers and refines the underlying motion, then renders the refined motion as 3D mesh and transfers facial appearance onto it, thereby improving motion accuracy and identity consistency. translated_abstract: 视频生成模型在合成逼真人体动作方面的能力日益增强，但它们往往丢失了使动作显得合理的关键结构信息。随着生成的人体动作变得更加复杂，视频可能出现逐帧累积的身体变形和外观漂移。现有的运动控制方法使用显式表示来稳定生成过程，但通常依赖预先定义的动作序列作为参考。这就引出了一个根本性问题：如果基础生成器已经能够产生可用的粗略动作，为什么还要用外部的动作来替代它？ReMoVe 通过将粗略输出视为一个“运动假设”而非最终结果来回答这一问题。ReMoVe 恢复并精炼底层运动，然后将精炼后的运动渲染为3D网格，并将面部外观迁移到其上，从而提升动作准确性和身份一致性。我们还进一步从同一3D……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出 ReMoVe 方法，将视频生成模型自身输出的粗略动作视为“运动假设”，通过恢复并精炼该动作、将其渲染为3D网格并迁移面部外观，从而在无需外部动作参考的情况下提升人体视频的动作准确性与身份一致性。
en_tdlr: ReMoVe treats the base video model's own coarse motion output as a motion hypothesis rather than a final result, recovering and refining it into a 3D mesh with transferred facial appearance to improve motion accuracy and identity consistency without relying on external motion references.
